NONE: › father: used by some South Asians to show respect to an older man
父親（南亞人對老年男性的稱呼，以示尊重）
› used by some South Asians when talking to a friend or a child, especially a man or boy
某些南亞人對朋友或兒童的稱謂（尤指男人或男孩）

I or T: › [ I or T ] to talk or say something in a quick, confused, excited, or silly way
牙牙學語，含糊不清地說；興奮地說；胡言亂語

I: › [ I ] literary (of a stream) to make the low, continuous noise of water flowing over stones

NONE: › a continuous low or confused sound, especially the sound of several people talking
亂哄哄的聲音（尤指多人唧唧喳喳的說話聲）

example: The children babbled excitedly among themselves.
孩子們聚在一起，興奮地說個沒完沒了。
She was babbling something about her ring being stolen.
她含糊不清地說著話，好像是說她的戒指被人偷了。
They rested a while by a babbling brook.
他們在潺潺作響的小溪邊休息了一會兒。
I could hear the babble of voices in the next room.
我可以聽到隔壁房裡的嘈雜聲。

NONE: › literary a small baby
嬰兒，嬰孩
› informal a word you can use when you are talking to someone you love such as your wife, husband, partner, etc.
寶貝（對妻子、丈夫、情人等的稱呼）
› informal a sexually attractive young person
有魅力的年輕人

example: a newborn babe
新生兒
It's up to you, babe. I'll do whatever you say.
寶貝，你來決定吧。你說甚麼我就做甚麼。
He's a total babe.
他可真是個小帥哥。

NONE: › a very young baby
繈褓中的嬰兒
› the confusing sound of many people talking at the same time or using different languages
嘈雜，喧嘩，混亂

example: a babel of voices
人聲嘈雜

NONE: › a type of large monkey, found in Africa and Asia, with a long, pointed face like a dog and large teeth
狒狒
A1 a very young child, especially one that has not yet begun to walk or talk
（尤指尚未學會走路或說話的）嬰兒，嬰孩
› to treat an older child as if he or she were a much younger child
把…當嬰兒般對待；對…嬌生慣養
A2 a very young animal
幼畜；幼獸；幼鳥
› disapproving an adult or especially an older child who is crying or behaving like a child
孩子氣的人；幼稚的人
› mainly US a word you can use when you are talking to someone you love such as your wife, husband, partner, etc.
寶貝（對妻子、丈夫、情人等的稱呼）
› a type of vegetable that is specially grown to stay small
迷你型胡蘿蔔（玉米等）
› informal Someone's baby is something that they have a special interest in and responsibility for.
（某人特別的或專門的）任務，差事；責任

example: a newborn baby
新生兒
a six-week-old baby
六週大的嬰兒
a baby boy
男嬰
Sandra had a baby (= gave birth to it) on 29 May.
桑德拉在5月29日生了孩子。
Owen is the baby (= the youngest person) of the family.
奧雲是家中年齡最小的。
a baby elephant/monkey
幼象／小猴子
It didn't hurt that much - don't be such a baby!
不至於那麼痛——別像個孩子似的！
Oh baby, I love you.
噢，寶貝，我愛你。
I don't know much about the project - it's Philip's baby.
我不是很清楚這個專案——那是菲力浦負責的。
The boys were now ten and twelve and didn't want their mother to baby them.
男孩們現在一個10歲，一個12歲，不希望媽媽把他們當作嬰兒看待。

NONE: › a feeling of sadness that some women experience after they have given birth to a baby
部分女性在分娩後經歷的一種憂鬱情緒；產後憂鬱症

example: According to this article, as many as 60 percent of women suffer from the baby blues.
這篇文章顯示，高達60%的女性有產後憂鬱症。

NONE: › a large increase in the number of babies born among a particular group of people during a particular time
生育高峰，嬰兒潮

example: There was a baby boom in the UK and the US after the Second World War.
二次世界大戰後，英國和美國都出現了一次嬰兒潮。

NONE: › a vehicle for moving a baby around that consists of a small bed supported by a frame on four wheels
手推童車，嬰兒車

example: I saw her pushing a baby carriage down the street.
我看見她推著嬰兒車沿著街道走。

NONE: › fat that a child sometimes has that disappears as the child grows older
兒童時期的肥胖（長大後即消失）

example: He's a little overweight but it's just baby fat.
他有點超重，不過這只是一時的幼年肥胖。

NONE: formula ( MILK FOR BABIES)
› a type of milk that can be given to babies instead of milk from their mother
（用以替代母乳的）嬰兒奶粉
› an act that makes a very small amount of progress towards achieving something
（向成功邁進的）一小步

example: Olympic officials have already started to take baby steps to rein in costs.
奧運會官員們已經在控制支出方面獲得了一些小的成功。

NONE: › the words that a very young child uses, or the words used by adults when they talk to babies
兒語；（成人對嬰兒用的）模仿兒語
› one of the teeth of young children and some other young mammals that fall out and are replaced by permanent teeth
乳牙
› a person who was born during a baby boom, especially the one that happened in the UK and the US following the Second World War
（尤指1945至1965年間英國和美國）嬰兒潮時代出生的人
› a brand name for a piece of clothing for a baby that covers the whole body
（包裹嬰兒全身、只露出頭、手的）嬰兒連身服
› the period of time when you are a baby
嬰兒時代，幼兒期
› only suitable for a baby
孩子氣的；幼稚的

example: The older children found the toys too babyish.
大一點的孩子覺得這些玩具太幼稚了。

NONE: B1 to take care of someone's baby or child while that person is out, usually by going to the person's home
（去別人家）代人臨時照顧孩子，當臨時保姆
› US UK childmind to take care of other people's children in your own home as a job
（在自己家）照管他人孩子（作為職業）

example: I babysit for Jane on Tuesday evenings while she goes to her yoga class.
每逢週二晚上簡去練習瑜伽時，我都替她看孩子。
Who babysits them when you're at work?
你上班的時候誰照看他們？

NONE: B1 someone who takes care of your baby or child while you are out, usually by coming to your home, especially someone you pay to do this
保姆（受僱代外出父母照料小孩的人）
› US UK childminder a person whose job is to take care of other people's children in her or his own home
（在自己家中照顧別人小孩的）保姆，保育員（通常為女性）

example: I promised the babysitter that we'd be home by midnight.
我向臨時保姆保證，我們一定會在午夜前回家。
I dropped the kids off at the babysitter's.
我把孩子們送到保姆家。
